NEW DELHI: BJP on Sunday criticised the Congress after stand-up comedian Pulkit Mani mimicked Prime Minister Narendra Modi during an event attended by party leader Rahul Gandhi in Madhya Pradesh, with Union ministers and other BJP leaders targeting the opposition party and Congress MP over the performance.The comedian performed the skit with the Rae Bareli MP during the latest edition of the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Indore on Saturday. A video of the performance was shared by the Congress on X.In the short act, Mani came on stage laughing and hugged Rahul. “My friend. How are you?” he said. The Congress leader replied, “I'm fine; how are you, Modi ji?” Mani responded, “Great harassment”, and continued laughing while repeatedly using the phrase “my friend”.Rahul then said, “Very nice to meet you,” and asked Mani to “tell me more”. The comedian continued laughing and hugging Gandhi before saying, “Maa ko kursi do, maa”, while pointing towards the audience.Union minister Piyush Goyal reacted to the performance on X, calling Rahul “Asanskari naraz fufa (uncultured disgruntled uncle).”“The irony writes itself. The need to come on stage every now and then just to drag Prime Minister Modi ji's name into cheap political theatre never fails to amaze me,” Goyal said, asking the former Congress president to “look in the mirror”.Union minister Kiren Rijiju also criticised Rahul, saying, “I hadn't imagined that a party which was in power for nearly six decades would turn into such a circus that is busy entertaining their own shrunken supporters.”Rijiju said Indians were proud that Prime Minister Modi was the “most popular” elected leader in the world.“Congress party has become a party of comedians and Jokers! They are out forever.... RIP,” he said.“Do you feel absolutely no shame in mocking an elderly mother and the Prime Minister of India?” Rijiju asked Rahul, while posting a video of PM Modi in which the prime minister is seen asking for a chair for an elderly woman who had attended one of his programmes.BJP national general secretary Smriti Irani also reacted to the controversy, writing in Hindi on X, “Jab nash manuj per chata hai, pehle vivek mar jaata hai” (When doom looms over a person, it's his conscience that dies first).BJP national secretary Sandeep Pathak called the mimicry act an expression of “desperation” and the “growing intellectual bankruptcy” of the Congress.“When you lose touch with India's values, you lose touch with India itself. And that is precisely where the Congress has lost its way,” Pathak, a Rajya Sabha MP, said on X.Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel hit back at the BJP's criticism, saying every person's mother deserved respect and questioning why similar concerns were not raised when the mothers of Rahul and other leaders were allegedly insulted.“Everyone's mother is a mother, not PM Modi's mother alone. Why are their feelings not hurt when they insult Rahul Gandhi's mother or other leaders' mothers? This culture of insulting mothers was started by BJP-RSS and Mahamanav,” Baghel said.Congress MP Imraan Masood said the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme had “shattered eardrums” of BJP leaders.“Let the elections come. They will find out soon enough. 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' has shattered their eardrums. They see Rahul Gandhi in their dreams and wake up with a start,” Masood said in Ranchi.Congress leader TS Singh Deo said criticism and mimicry should not be objected to, but opposed the use of abusive language in public conversations.“I do not think it is acceptable to stoop to the level of abusive language in a public conversation. NEW DELHI: With Uttar Pradesh set for assembly polls in 2027, AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi has thrown open the possibility of an alliance with parties looking to prevent the BJP from returning to power for a third straight term, saying no opposition party can take on the BJP alone.Owaisi, speaking to news agency ANI on Sunday, invited “like-minded” parties for talks and said AIMIM was prepared to work with them if the common objective was to keep the BJP out of power.“We do not want the BJP government to be formed for a third time in Uttar Pradesh. If anyone does not want the BJP to form the government, they can talk to us. We are ready to work with you to stop the BJP from coming to power. But it is important to understand that you cannot stop the BJP alone,” he said.His outreach comes as political parties begin preparing for the 2027 contest in Uttar Pradesh, where the BJP has been in power since 2017 under the leadership of Yogi Adityanath Owaisi, however, cautioned against viewing the coming election through the lens of previous polls, saying the political contest would have its own set of challenges.“Assembly elections are coming. It won’t be the 2014 election, nor the 2017 election, nor the 2019 election, nor the 2022 election.This is going to be a completely different election,” he said.Owaisi pointed to AIMIM’s experience in Bihar to underline the party’s position on alliances. He said the party had approached several opposition leaders before the Bihar elections , seeking an alliance and asking for six seats, but the proposal did not find support.“We said this in Bihar as well, and our president, Akhtarul Iman, wrote a letter not just to the RJD or the Congress, but to all the CPI and Communist Party leaders. We said, ‘Please give us six seats.’ But they did not agree,” he said.Despite the lack of an alliance, Owaisi said AIMIM would continue building its organisation in Uttar Pradesh. He claimed the party’s leadership had developed from the grassroots and said its workers were already active across constituencies.“Our party organisation has become quite strong. Our leadership has emerged at the grassroots level, and our leaders have a strong connection with the ground. The party is working hard on its part,” he said.Hyderabad MP said alliance talks would not determine AIMIM’s organisational plans.“Whether we are in talks with whom or not is a different matter, but we will continue our work. If you want to stop the BJP, come and talk to us. We are ready to work with you,” he said.Turning to the Yogi-led BJP government, Owaisi alleged that several promises made by the party remained unfulfilled. He raised issues including governance, law and order, electricity and land disputes, saying these would become important themes in the election.He also criticised the previous Samajwadi Party government, drawing a comparison between the two regimes.“When the Samajwadi Party was in power, one kind of hooliganism used to happen. Someone else did it. Now, under their government, a different kind of hooliganism is happening,” Owaisi said.He also sought the public release of the SIT report into the alleged Ram Mandir embezzlement case and questioned how accused persons were securing bail.“Why isn’t the SIT report released to the public? Why doesn’t the government release it? And why are those people getting bail? How are they getting bail? It’s strange. This will also be a big talking point,” he said.AIMIM has already begun preparing for the 2027 election, with Owaisi saying the party is touring constituencies to strengthen its organisation and gauge local concerns.He said he was in Kanpur on Sunday and would visit Shravasti in six days, followed by Azamgarh. Public meetings are also planned in three or four constituencies in western Uttar Pradesh.“The sole purpose is to strengthen our party organisation for the upcoming elections,” Owaisi said.He added that staying connected with voters was central to the party’s preparations.“By staying among the people, we can understand their suffering on the ground and highlight the difficulties this government has created for them,” he said.
Article Summary: AIMIM supremo Asaduddin Owaisi has thrown open the possibility of an alliance with parties looking to prevent the BJP from returning to power for a third straight term. He invited ‘like-minded’ parties for talks and said AIMIM was prepared to work with them if the common objective was to keep the BJP out of power.

NEW DELHI: BJP stalwart LK Advani and former Delhi deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia are among the prominent voters whose names figure in the list of 33 lakh people being issued notices over “logical discrepancies” in details furnished during the recent Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Delhi.“The notices arose from ‘logical discrepancies’ in the details furnished in their enumeration forms. Their names will be included in the final electoral rolls after due process of verification of facts and documents to be furnished by such voters,” a senior poll officer told PTI, confirming that notices had been issued to both Advani and Sisodia.“The process of verification of facts and documents is underway and validation of entries is being done accordingly,” the officer added.The 98-year-old Advani, a former deputy prime minister, his daughter Pratibha and daughter-in-law Geetika also received notices after their names could not be mapped to the 2002 SIR electoral roll. His son, Jayant, however, cleared the mapping exercise.All four are registered voters in the New Delhi assembly constituency.Meanwhile, in Sisodia’s family, his wife Seema and son Meer have also been issued notices.While the Election Commission has not cited a specific reason for the notice issued to the AAP leader, his son Meer’s notice mentions a “discrepancy in his parent’s name”, according to officials. The notice issued to his wife, Seema, cites a “mismatch in her own name”.Many prominent voters, including senior government functionaries, bureaucrats and politicians, have been issued notices as part of the SIR exercise in Delhi.Chief minister Rekha Gupta, AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal and former Union minister Kapil Sibal have also received notices over similar discrepancies, officials said.Gupta’s entry was validated following verification of her documents, and her name has been cleared for inclusion in the final electoral roll of the Shalimar Bagh constituency, scheduled to be published on November 4.According to the Delhi CEO’s office, notices are being issued to voters whose names could not be linked to the electoral roll prepared during the previous SIR, or whose details showed discrepancies when matched against the earlier roll.As part of the door-to-door verification exercise conducted between June 30 and August 17, every voter was required to submit an enumeration form.Of the around 97 lakh voters included in the draft electoral rolls, 33.13 lakh have been identified for notices over discrepancies in their enumeration forms. More than 31.63 lakh notices have been served so far.Most of the notices relate to the absence of corresponding records in the electoral roll prepared during the previous SIR in 2002.Voters have been asked to submit their replies along with supporting documents to the Electoral Registration Officers of their respective Assembly constituencies by October 29.
Article Summary: LK Advani and Manish Sisodia are among the prominent voters whose names figure in the list of 33 lakh people being issued notices. Article Title: Delhi pollution crackdown: Hotspots to be mapped, pending road works get Oct 31 deadline
Article Text:
A thick layer of smog engulfs the India Gate and Kartavya Path as pollution level deteriorates, in New Delhi.

Hotspots to get source-specific action plans

October 31 target for pending road works

Construction, waste burning face tighter action

Illegal parking and encroachments targeted

Patparganj gets special focus

Future roads to minimise exposed soil

NEW DELHI: The Delhi government has stepped up its crackdown on air pollution, directing district administrations to map pollution hotspots, identify sources within a three-kilometre radius and assign agencies specific corrective measures and deadlines. The government has also set October 31 as the target for completing pending road and civil works, wherever feasible. It ordered tighter action against road dust, construction pollution, waste burning, illegal parking and traffic congestion.The directions were issued during district-level review meetings chaired by Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa for East, North-East, South-East and South Delhi. Officials were told to use AQI monitoring data to identify problem areas, assess the sources driving pollution and take immediate action at the ground level.District administrations will map pollution hotspots based on data from AQI monitoring stations. Each hotspot will then be assessed for sources such as road dust, traffic congestion, vehicular emissions, construction and demolition activity, unauthorised parking, open or uncovered areas and biomass or waste burning.Where applicable, pollution-generating activities within a three-kilometre radius of each hotspot will also be examined.Authorities will prepare source-wise action plans setting out the remedial measure, the agency responsible and the timeline for implementation.Locations recording high levels of PM10 and PM2.5 will receive focused attention, particularly areas with heavy traffic, heavy-vehicle parking, significant road dust and congestion. Such locations will be inspected for their pollution sources and immediate remedial action will be taken.The government has directed agencies to complete pending civil works on priority and by October 31, wherever feasible.These include pothole repairs, treatment and development of brown areas and other road and roadside works. Officials have also been told to maintain completed works properly to reduce road-dust generation.Where essential works cannot be completed because other projects are still underway, agencies will have to continue water sprinkling and other dust-suppression measures until the road surface is restored.The government has directed agencies to strictly enforce dust-control norms at construction and demolition sites. Violations will attract stringent action under applicable rules.The ban on biomass burning will also be enforced without exception. Preventive measures will be strengthened against the open burning of garbage, plastic and rubber waste, textile and fibre waste, industrial and organic residues, scrap and other combustible material.Officials were also directed to remove illegal encroachments from roads and public spaces where they contribute to congestion and obstruct traffic movement.The move is aimed at improving traffic flow and reducing pollution caused by idling vehicles and prolonged traffic movement.At Anand Vihar Bus Terminal, agencies have been directed to step up enforcement against unauthorised parking of buses and heavy vehicles. Cranes will be deployed wherever required to remove or tow such vehicles.Patparganj Industrial Area was identified for area-specific measures targeting road dust, traffic congestion and vehicular emissions.Agencies have been directed to maintain continuous water sprinkling and dust-control measures at vulnerable locations, particularly where road or allied works are underway.For future applicable works, departments have been directed to incorporate end-to-end carpeting or paving of roads and relevant roadside areas wherever technically feasible and in accordance with applicable specifications.The aim is to reduce exposed soil and unpaved surfaces that can contribute to road dust.The government has stressed closer coordination between departments and agencies, with responsibility for individual pollution-control measures clearly assigned.The meetings involved area MLAs, district magistrates, deputy commissioners of police, MCD deputy commissioners and senior officials from various departments.Officials from the Revenue Department, DPCC, PWD, MCD, Traffic Police, DSIIDC, I&FC, DJB, DMRC, NHAI and other agencies were involved in the coordinated effort.The minister also directed ground teams to maintain regular vigilance at vulnerable locations and take immediate action against violations. DPCC and enforcement agencies were asked to impose stringent penalties, including heavy challans wherever applicable.Officials were further told to ensure prompt resolution of citizen complaints, particularly those received through Helpline 311.
Article Summary: District administrations will map pollution hotspots based on data from AQI monitoring stations. Each hotspot will be assessed for sources such as road dust, traffic congestion, vehicular emissions, construction and demolition activity, unauthorised parking, open or uncovered areas and biomass or waste burning.
